The regression test phase passed 20 of 20 checks with no bugs filed, and that completes the whole suite: all 9 test phases are `done`, with no bugs and no stories left out.

- **R1–R17:** I didn't re-run these. They rely on the previous session's results from earlier today (17:25–18:07), which also ran on a fresh database. That session crashed before writing its report, but its logs, JSON results and screenshots are complete. The session before it (15:05–15:12) also crashed, and its files are not used as evidence. The report says all of this.
- **R18 and R19 (frontend Polish and Convergence):** I re-ran these in the headless browser, on the fresh database the runner started at 21:46. Every UI selector in the contract was present once there was data. Every error and notice message appeared. A plan that started while the page was open showed its "Started" badge and notice right at its start time (21:49:43). The Dashboard showed exactly what the API returned. Clicking all six navigation links reached the right pages with no console errors. There are no leftover spec files, and the dev build shows no errors.
- **R20 (unit tests):** all 338 backend tests passed. Line coverage of the domain code is 97.3% (676 of 695 lines), above the 80% threshold. I worked that out from the jacoco report because the runner's own coverage check wrongly reports "skipped": it misses the `domain.*` sub-packages, as in every earlier run.

Things I noted but didn't file as bugs:
- **Display name "GG":** the Dashboard greeting read "Hello, GG" because the settings API returned that name. This session never changed the settings, so something outside it (possibly a manual visit to the app) set it after the fresh start. The greeting correctly showed what the API returned.
- **Plan status label:** at the exact moment the "Started" badge appeared, the plan's status label still said "Not Started". It switched to "In Progress" a few seconds later without a reload. The previous US6 test phase saw the same short delay.
- **Not run by design:** the backend restart check, because the testing loop never stops or starts processes.
